increment_paragraph: **OPENSSL-BIO-METHODS-AND-CALLBACKS (2026-11-19).** User decision 2026-11-19 launches the follow-up OPENSSL-UNDECLARED-HANDSHAKE-CALLBACKS recorded. BIO_free read silently that dropping a BIO's last reference runs its callback (BIO_CB_FREE), its method's destroy function and the BIO class's ex_data free callbacks; it now names the premise openssl_bio_free_callbacks (C04.18), as SSL_free does for the BIOs it frees. Stating the invocation was checked and not done: C04.19 rejects a callback clause beside a reference drop, and lifting that check alone is unsound because a candidate's requirement on the dropped formal is applied by the callback route after the reference route in the transfer (OPENSSL-FREE-SESSION-REMOVE-INVOCATION, whose discharge now includes these invocations). quirin-provider-openssl states fourteen more opaque slots (C04.19.3, rule 12n amended in place): a BIO's callback (bio_st.bio_callback_ex, bio_st.bio_callback) and one key per function of a method table (bio_method_st.meth_write_ex ... meth_recvmmsg), each written by the one setter its 3.5 page names (new module bio_slots.qv, 14 setters; two page snapshots added, prototypes pinned, every existing entry byte-identical). The method table is a holder-to-holder slot: its holder is the BIO_METHOD a setter is handed, which reaches the SSL through BIO_new and SSL_set_bio; the key is run-wide, so the set is every function any table's setter is handed, beside the built-in methods, which the new library-value premise openssl_builtin_bio_methods names. SSL_write/read/connect/do_handshake and SSL_shutdown invoke all fourteen on ssl with every actual _ (41 and 17 invocations); openssl_unstated_callback_slots drops the BIOs from its statement. Keys are named after their setters: a first tip run with the library's field names (ctrl, create, destroy, callback) found every BIO key open, since rule 12n's pre-pass then read units naming those generic tokens, among them wasm_loader.c, whose AST exceeds the reader's recursion limit and so also opened rd_kafka_op_s.rko_op_cb and moved 6 rows Safe to Unknown (fail-closed, evidence kept). ledger.why: OPENSSL-BIO-METHODS-AND-CALLBACKS (2026-11-19): a BIO's callback and the twelve functions of its method table are stated opaque slots with every writer their 3.5 pages name (14 setters in bio_slots.qv), the method table read as a holder-to-holder slot (run-wide key, BIO_METHOD holder reaching the SSL through BIO_new and SSL_set_bio) beside the library-value premise openssl_builtin_bio_methods for the built-in methods; the four handshake and I/O calls and SSL_shutdown invoke all fourteen, and openssl_unstated_callback_slots no longer names the BIOs. BIO_free (and SSL_free) name openssl_bio_free_callbacks for the callback, destroy function and ex_data free callbacks a BIO's last drop runs; stating those invocations waits on OPENSSL-FREE-SESSION-REMOVE-INVOCATION's clause beside a drop (appended there). ledger.title: The PEM and PKCS#12 BIO readers run the BIO's callback and methods unstated
ledger.text: PEM_read_bio_X509, PEM_read_bio_PrivateKey and d2i_PKCS12_bio read through the caller's BIO, so they run its callback (bio_st.bio_callback_ex / bio_callback: 'called during most high-level BIO operations', BIO_set_callback 3.5) and its method table's read, gets and ctrl functions (bio_method_st.*), and their declarations neither state that nor name a premise for it. The slots are stated since OPENSSL-BIO-METHODS-AND-CALLBACKS, but a slot invocation cannot stand beside these declarations' literal-argument premise (rule 57: 'a literal-argument premise stands beside a synchronous invocation only'). DISCHARGE: admit a slot invocation beside a literal-argument premise (rule 57 amended, the invocation decided only at calls the premise holds for) and state the BIO slots on the readers with openssl_builtin_bio_methods, or name a premise for them; Lean beside QCore.OpensslBioSlots. Size: small to medium.

OPENSSL-BIO-METHODS-AND-CALLBACKS adds to the same discharge: BIO_free and SSL_free run a BIO's callback (bio_st.bio_callback_ex, bio_callback, with BIO_CB_FREE and the BIO as `a`) and its destroy function (bio_method_st.meth_destroy) beside their reference drop, now covered by openssl_bio_free_callbacks; once a slot invocation stands beside a drop (the candidates' requirements on the dropped formal applied before the drop, which legacy_transfer.rs orders after it today), state them there and narrow that premise to the ex_data free callbacks.
Since OPENSSL-BIO-METHODS-AND-CALLBACKS the BIOs are stated slots, so after this card the premise names only the ctrl arms, CT and ex_data.
